units.text: INT. OBSERVATORY DOME - NIGHT
A brass telescope as long as a bus points at a slit of stars.
The floor is parquet, the walls lined with star charts and one tipped-over teacup.
On the floor beside the eyepiece platform lies a coat, empty, its sleeves flung wide.
Five people stand in a loose ring around it, and nobody wants to be the first to look down.
HENRIETTA "HETTY" BLACKWOOD (60s, observatory director, tweed, a magnifying glass on a chain) stares at the coat.
BASTIAN ODUYA (30s, graduate student, ink on his fingers, a wool hat pulled low).
SOLEDAD "SOLI" VARGAS (40s, night technician, thermos in one hand and the dome keys in the other).
WILFRED PRATT (70s, retired astronomer, a cane, a rumpled evening jacket).
And MEI-LING TAN (20s, journalist, notebook, recorder held out like a candle).
Who last saw Doctor Marrow?
units.name: HETTY

units.text: Soli did. She locked up at nine.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: I locked the north door. I did not lock the dome.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: Soledad, my dear, a dome has no door. It is a lid.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Then I locked the lid, Mr. Pratt.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: Let's slow down. Soli, you said Doctor Marrow asked you for the keys?
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: He asked. I said no.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: You told me you gave them to him.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: I told you he asked, Bash. You heard what you wanted.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: Bastian. Where were you at nine?
units.name: HETTY

units.text: Plate room. Cataloguing.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: For five hours? That's not cataloguing, it's meditation.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: It was the Hartwell plates, Mr. Pratt. You know how many there are.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: I know how many there were. I counted them in 1989.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Mr. Pratt, you told me earlier you hadn't been to the observatory in years.
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: Did I?
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Your exact words were, "I haven't set foot on this hill since the Marrow appointment."
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: Then I was speaking figuratively.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Wilfred. You have a key.
units.name: HETTY

units.text: Everyone has a key, Hetty. That's the tragedy of the institution.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: I don't think everyone has a key.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: Soli, who does?
units.name: HETTY

units.text: Me. You. Doctor Marrow.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: And Pratt, apparently.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: Apparently.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: So four keys. And a coat on the floor.
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: Don't touch the coat, Miss Tan.
units.name: HETTY

units.text: I wasn't going to.
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: You were. You've been inching toward it for five minutes.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: I'm a reporter. Inching is the job.
units.name: MEI-LING

units.text: Inching is how the best of us died, my girl.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Wilfred, enough.
units.name: HETTY

units.text: I'm only saying. The coat is on the floor, the lid is open, and Doctor Marrow is not in either of them. Somebody in this room is going to have to explain that. And I would very much like for it not to be me.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Then explain why your cane is wet.
units.name: BASTIAN

units.text: A silence.
The telescope creaks.
It rained.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: It hasn't rained since Tuesday.
units.name: SOLI

units.text: Wilfred.
units.name: HETTY

units.text: Hetty.
units.name: PRATT

units.text: Where is he?
units.name: HETTY
